correctness.rationale: Contractive multipliers satisfy ||phi||_H<=1 by acting on the constant; weighted monomial Cauchy-Schwarz and an exact multinomial series prove the ball inclusion. The explicit degree-two Blaschke product composed with a norm-one directional coordinate multiplier is contractive by von Neumann functional calculus and realizes rt/(1-rt), establishing each pointwise boundary/exclusion. At r²=1/2, expansion of the positive weighted coefficient square gives the exact deficit and equality profile; analytic convergence in countably many coordinates uses finite truncation and monotone convergence. Exact rational tests support finite coefficient identities but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The zero-at-origin constrained Bohr set is a mathematically natural anchored companion to the recently characterized unrestricted multiplier set. The result classifies the entire admissible set for all finite multivariable dimensions and countably infinite dimension, constructs nonlinear norm-one extremizers at every multicoordinate boundary point, and gives an exact weighted coefficient-modulus stability/equality law, rather than a mere fixed-number constant or finite computational example.
